articles.title: Make the weekly project review worth your time
articles.summary: Start with what changed, find the work that needs a decision, and leave with a clear next step.
articles.alt: The Studio North overview, with completion history, recent activity and project results.
articles.caption: The overview brings project health and recent changes into one view.

sections.title: Start with what changed
paragraphs: A project review is most useful when it helps the team decide what to do next. Reading every status aloud leaves little room for that conversation. Begin with the changes since your last review instead.

In Tandem, the overview pairs completed tasks with recent activity. Choose the same reporting period each time you meet, then use the activity list to find the projects behind those changes. A busy chart tells you that work happened; the project details tell you what still needs attention.

sections.title: Find the decisions hiding in the list
paragraphs: Switch to the project table when you need to compare owners, due dates and progress. Filter to work in review, or sort by due date to bring approaching commitments together. Open a project when its summary raises a question.

Progress and status answer different questions. A project can have most of its tasks finished and still need a review. Treat the percentage as context, then ask what would let the project move forward.
bullets: Does the owner have what they need to finish?
Is the due date still realistic?
Who needs to review the work before it can be completed?

sections.title: Leave with a next step
paragraphs: Update the owner or due date while the decision is fresh. Move a project into review when it is ready for that conversation. Mark it complete only when the team agrees the work is finished: in the demo, that also completes its remaining tasks.
For your next review, return to the same view and filters. A useful routine makes changes easy to spot without turning the meeting into another reporting exercise.

articles.title: Table, cards or board? Start with the question.
articles.summary: Three views of the same projects, each suited to a different kind of decision.
articles.alt: Projects arranged into In progress, In review and Completed columns in Tandem.
articles.caption: The board groups the same project records by their current status.

sections.title: Compare details in a table
paragraphs: Use the table when you have a specific question: which projects are due soon, who owns them, or how far along they are. Columns line up the answers so you can scan across several projects without opening each one.
Keep the columns you need for the decision. Search, owner and status filters reduce the list; sorting changes its order. Hiding a column does not change which projects match.

sections.title: Browse the work with cards
paragraphs: Cards give each project room for its description. They work well when you are getting familiar with a workspace or looking for a project whose name you do not quite remember.
The owner, due date and progress remain visible, while the description supplies context. Open the project for the full details rather than trying to make every card carry the entire record.

sections.title: Move work forward on a board
paragraphs: The board answers a different question: where is work waiting? Projects sit in In progress, In review or Completed. Drag a card to another column, or use its menu to change status without dragging.
Moving into Completed finishes any remaining tasks. Moving a completed project back reopens its status and preserves its completed tasks. The table, cards and overview all reflect the same change.

articles.title: Give every project a clear handoff
articles.summary: A named owner, a useful description and a realistic date make the next person's job easier.
articles.alt: Brand refresh project details showing its owner, due date, progress and recent activity.
articles.caption: A project record keeps the essentials together for its next owner.

sections.title: Name the outcome
paragraphs: A short project name should help someone recognize the work in a list. Use the description to explain the outcome and the boundaries: what will be different when this is finished, and what is outside this project?
The next person should be able to open the record and understand why the work exists. A paragraph of useful context is more valuable than a long description that repeats the title.

sections.title: Choose an owner
paragraphs: Ownership gives the team a person to turn to for the next decision. It does not mean that person has to do every task. Pick the person who can keep the work moving and coordinate a review when it is ready.

When several projects move to a new owner, select them in Projects and use Assign owner. If a member is removed from the team, Tandem asks for a replacement owner for their projects so the work remains assigned.

sections.title: Make the date useful
paragraphs: Set a due date that represents the team's current commitment. If that commitment changes, update the record so everyone sees the same expectation. A date that nobody believes is less useful than an honest adjustment.
Before handing the project over, check the description, owner and date together. Then leave the record in the status that reflects the work still to do.

guides.title: Explore the demo and reset your changes
guides.summary: What you can change, what stays on this device, and how to start again.

sections.title: Try the sample workspace
paragraphs: Open demo to enter Studio North. You can create and edit projects, move work on the board, update your profile and manage the sample team. These changes apply to your current browser session.
The sample workspace uses a fixed snapshot date. Its charts, deadlines and activity demonstrate a workflow rather than reporting live work.

sections.title: Know what is saved
paragraphs: Project, profile, team and workspace changes reset when you reload. Navigating between pages keeps those changes, including unfinished form drafts. Appearance preferences are different: theme, font, density and accent choices are saved on this device when browser storage is available.
Sign-up and password recovery are local examples. They do not create a real account or send email. Sample pricing does not charge you or restrict the demo's features.

sections.title: Start again
paragraphs: Choose Reset demo data in the workspace sidebar to restore the sample workspace and clear its drafts. On a narrow screen, open the navigation menu to find that action.
To reset the look of the interface as well, open Appearance and choose Restore defaults. Resetting the workspace does not change your appearance preferences.

guides.title: Create and edit a project
guides.summary: Set a name, owner and due date, and understand how drafts behave.

sections.title: Create a project
paragraphs: Choose New project from Overview or Projects. Give the project a recognizable name, select its owner and choose a due date. The description is optional.
steps: Enter the project's name and, if useful, a short description of the intended outcome.
Choose an owner from the workspace members and set the due date.
Choose Create project. The new project is available in the shared project views.

sections.title: Edit the details
paragraphs: Open a project's name to see its full page, then choose Edit project. You can also open the inspector and choose Edit project there. Saving updates the same record in the list, board, inspector and activity.
If a required field is missing or a value needs attention, the form identifies the field. Correct it and save again; the other entered values stay in place.

sections.title: Keep or discard a draft
paragraphs: Navigating away keeps an unfinished draft for the current session. Return to the create or edit page to continue. Cancel explicitly discards that form's draft, and a successful save clears it.
Reloading or using Reset demo data clears all demo drafts. Save any information you need outside the demo before reloading; it has no permanent project storage.

guides.title: Change a project's status
guides.summary: Move work on the board, complete projects and reopen them when needed.

sections.title: Use the board
paragraphs: Open Projects and choose Board. Each column represents a status: In progress, In review or Completed. Search and filters still apply, so a filtered board may show only part of the workspace.
steps: Find the project you want to move.
Drag its card into the destination column, or open the card's dot menu and choose the destination status.
The project moves to that status and the other project views update with it.

sections.title: Complete or reopen work
paragraphs: Moving into Completed also completes the project's remaining tasks. The same rule applies to Mark complete in the details and bulk actions.
Moving a completed project back to In progress or In review changes its status while keeping its completed tasks. Its progress can therefore remain at 100% while its status is open.

sections.title: When a card leaves your results
paragraphs: If your view is filtered to one status, a project moved to another status no longer matches. Clear the status filter or choose the new status to see it again. The project has not been deleted.
Use the Table or Cards view whenever comparing dates, owners or descriptions is more useful than grouping work by status.

guides.title: Manage members and project ownership
guides.summary: Invite a sample member, change a role or reassign projects before removing someone.

sections.title: Find team settings
paragraphs: Open the account menu at the bottom of the workspace navigation, choose Workspace settings, then Team. Members and pending invitations appear separately.

Choose Invite member to add a local pending invitation. Enter an email address, then choose a role. The demo checks for duplicate email addresses but does not send an invitation or provide an acceptance flow.

sections.title: Change a role
paragraphs: Use a member's row menu to change their role. At least one workspace owner must remain, so the sole owner cannot be demoted or removed.
These roles demonstrate the team-management workflow. They are not a production access-control system.

sections.title: Remove a member
paragraphs: Choose Remove member from the member's row menu. If they own projects, select a replacement owner before confirming. Reassignment and removal happen together, so their projects remain assigned.
Historical activity keeps the original person's name. Removing a member does not rewrite who performed earlier work. Leaving the workspace as the current account is outside this demo.

guides.title: Change the look and density of Tandem
guides.summary: Choose a theme, accent, font and layout that work for you.

sections.title: Open Appearance
paragraphs: In the workspace, choose Appearance in the sidebar or use the appearance control in the header. On public pages, the same control appears in the footer. You can also open the Appearance page from the account settings.
Changes apply immediately. There is no separate Save button for appearance preferences.

sections.title: Choose your settings
paragraphs: Use Light, Dark or System to choose how the interface follows your device's color scheme. Accent and font choices apply across the workspace and its overlays.

Comfortable and Compact change the spacing of supported controls and layouts. They do not change the project's data. Corners and header surface offer additional visual choices without changing the available actions.

sections.title: Restore defaults
paragraphs: Choose Restore defaults in Appearance to return to the initial visual settings. These preferences are stored on this device when browser storage is available.
Reset demo data restores projects and workspace data but preserves appearance. If preferences cannot be saved, Appearance reports that the change applies only to the current session.

releases.title: Delivery analytics
releases.summary: Analytics now shows whether work is finished as fast as it arrives: tasks completed and added, the change in open work, and how long tasks take.

sections.title: New
bullets: Analytics opens with Delivery: tasks completed and added over time, whether the backlog grew or shrank each day or week, and the median days from adding a task to completing it.
Turn on Compare with previous period to see each figure against the period just before, with last period's completions as a dashed line.
Choose Last 90 days to read the last three months by week. Hide a series from the chart's legend to focus on the other.

sections.title: Improved
bullets: Analytics is organised into Delivery and Projects and people, under one row of filters.
Charts with nothing to show in the chosen range now say so, instead of drawing a flat line.
Overview's chart offers Last 90 days too, read as weekly bars.

sections.title: Demo boundaries
paragraphs: The sample history starts on 26 June 2026, so comparisons need a period that starts after that. Everything resets on reload.

releases.title: Tasks added, and a longer history
releases.summary: The completion chart now shows tasks added as well as completed, and the sample workspace has three months of history behind it.

sections.title: Improved
bullets: Choose Completed or Added in the chart's heading on Overview and Analytics to see how fast work is finished and how fast it arrives. Show data lists both.
Every task now records the day it was added and the day it was completed, so longer ranges and the project timeline show the full three months of work.
Chart colours are arranged so neighbouring series stay distinguishable for colour-blind readers, with their own shades in dark mode.

sections.title: Demo boundaries
paragraphs: The history is sample data; tasks you add or complete join it until you reload.

releases.title: Agent runs on projects
releases.summary: Hand routine project work to the agent: it works through it in the background and asks before it posts or adds anything.

sections.title: New
bullets: A project's new Agent tab can write a status report or plan the launch. Watch each step and what it found, or leave the page while it works.
The agent stops for your review before it changes anything: edit the report and post it to Comments, or approve the tasks it proposes. Discard or Stop run leaves the project as it was.
If a step fails, try it again or continue without it. The tab is marked while a run needs you, and earlier runs stay available from the run picker.

sections.title: Improved
bullets: On wide screens, pages start at the left edge under the top bar instead of sitting in the middle with a gap on either side.

sections.title: Demo boundaries
paragraphs: Runs are scripted from your project's records, run in your browser and reset on reload. They aren't scheduled and don't notify you elsewhere.

releases.title: Calmer project pages
releases.summary: Project pages put the work first, with the details beside it; the projects list is lighter; and the assistant's history can step aside.

sections.title: Improved
bullets: Project pages are reorganised: progress and Mark complete sit beside the name; Tasks, Comments and Activity are tabs; and Project details and files sit in a column beside them.

Tasks switch between Open and Completed, and a task you tick stays in place until you change view. Open a task's name to read or edit its description, and add tasks in a dialog. Assignees' avatars line up, and only the checkbox completes a task.
Project pages, the editor and import lose their Back row: the breadcrumb names where you came from and takes you back there, and on phones a back arrow sits beside the title.
One Edit button beside a project's details changes the owner, due date, tags and links together in a dialog.
The projects list shows all your projects on one page by default, its filters and column headers stay quiet until you use them, and on phones its view controls share the filter row.
Hide the assistant's history to give the conversation the whole width; History in the top bar brings it back.
The navigation button in the top bar now lines up with the page below it.
While the assistant works on a reply or reasons through a question, its Thinking… label shimmers in colour, and the shimmer on plans moves faster so you can see it.

The assistant shows its plan for each request above the message box, ticking off steps as it works. A Conversation panel lists what it did for each question, the drafts and tasks it produced, and the pages it cited; select Thought for… on a reply to open it there.

sections.title: Demo boundaries
paragraphs: Everything runs in your browser and resets on reload.

releases.title: An assistant that knows your projects
releases.summary: Ask the Tandem Assistant about your workspace: it answers from your projects with sources, drafts status updates and adds tasks once you approve.

sections.title: Added
bullets: The Assistant answers questions about risk, this week and project status from your live projects, shows its reasoning and the searches it ran, and cites its sources.
It can add a checklist of tasks to a project. You see the plan first and approve it; nothing changes without your yes.
Draft a status update for any project, then copy it, download it or post it to the project as a comment.
Conversation history with rename and delete, earlier versions of a reply, and restoring a conversation to an earlier point.
Attach files and projects as context, choose a model and see how much of its context a conversation uses.
Settings › Assistant shows what the assistant does and lets you switch each of its tools off.
Every help guide offers Ask about this guide.

sections.title: Demo boundaries
paragraphs: Replies are scripted and run in your browser; no message reaches a real model. Tasks and comments the assistant adds reset on reload, like every other change.

releases.title: Tasks, timelines and a search for everything
releases.summary: Projects gain real task lists, comments and files; a Timeline view, saved views and workspace-wide search help you find the work.

sections.title: Added
bullets: Task lists on every project: add, complete, assign and reorder, with progress that follows along.
Comments with @mentions that reach the inbox, and files with previews.
A Timeline view with a month calendar, and saved views you can share by link.
Search across projects, tasks, comments, messages, people and help.
Import projects from a CSV file, and a getting-started list for new workspaces.

sections.title: Improved
bullets: Undo after completing, moving or deleting, and date pickers for due dates and custom report ranges.

sections.title: Demo boundaries
paragraphs: Everything runs in your browser and resets on reload. Uploads and imports stay in memory, and mentions of teammates send nothing.

releases.title: A public front door for the workspace
releases.summary: Explore the product, compare sample plans and get help with the demo.

sections.title: Added
bullets: Product previews link directly to the overview, board and project details.
Sample pricing offers monthly and annual periods, with the selected plan carried through local sign-up.
Articles, release notes and searchable help share the public navigation and appearance settings.

sections.title: Demo boundaries
paragraphs: Plan selection is illustrative. No checkout, payment or feature restriction is applied. Help search uses the included guides, and the release numbers on this page are sample content for the template.

releases.title: A workspace that feels like your team's
releases.summary: Profile, workspace and team settings, with drafts that stay with you while navigating.

sections.title: Added
bullets: Profile name, bio and local photo selection.
Workspace name and logo, with explicit Save and Cancel actions.
Member roles, local pending invitations and project reassignment during member removal.
Local sign-up, workspace setup and password-recovery examples.

sections.title: Behavior
paragraphs: The sole workspace owner cannot be removed or demoted. Removing a project owner requires a replacement, while historical activity keeps its original actor.
All workspace and account changes reset on reload. Invitations and recovery do not send email, and the example does not authenticate against an external service.

releases.title: Projects, from a quick scan to the full picture
releases.summary: A shared project workflow across the overview, table, cards and board.

sections.title: Added
bullets: Search, status and owner filters across project views.
Project details, creation and editing, with retained in-session drafts.
Bulk owner assignment and project completion.
Board status movement by dragging or using the project menu.

sections.title: Behavior
paragraphs: Completing a project also finishes its remaining tasks. Reopening it preserves completed tasks. Cancel discards the current form draft; navigating away keeps it until save, cancellation or reload.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.summary: Sample notice for this interactive demo. Replace it with a notice for your organisation and services before publishing a real product.

sections.title: Information you enter
paragraphs: Tandem is an interactive example with fictional workspace data. Project edits, profile details, team changes and form drafts are kept in memory for the current browser session. Reloading restores the sample workspace and clears those drafts.

Use sample details when exploring the forms. Contact messages are kept in memory while you navigate, then cleared when the demo submission completes or the demo is reset or reloaded. No contact message is sent to a recipient.

sections.title: Preferences on this device
paragraphs: Appearance preferences, including theme, font, accent and density, are saved in this browser's local storage when it is available. They allow the interface to keep your chosen appearance when you return.

You can use Restore defaults in Appearance to reset the settings. Clearing this site's browser storage removes the saved preferences. Reset demo data restores the sample workspace but leaves appearance preferences in place.

sections.title: Forms and external services
paragraphs: The included contact, newsletter, invitation and account flows run locally. They do not send messages, subscribe you to a mailing list, charge a payment method or create an account with an external service. Password fields are not saved by the application.
The included application does not load analytics or advertising integrations. Fonts and demo images are served with the site. Links to external sites take you to services with their own practices.

sections.title: A notice for a live service
paragraphs: This sample does not identify a real data controller, hosting provider or support team. A deployed site's hosting and any services added to it may process data separately from this browser demo.

Before launch, replace this sample with an accurate notice identifying the responsible organisation, its contact details, the information it uses and why, the applicable legal basis, recipients, retention periods, relevant transfers and people's rights. Confirm the notice against the actual deployment and applicable requirements.

terms.title: Terms
terms.summary: Sample terms page for the Tandem demo. Replace this specimen with terms suited to your organisation and service before launch.

sections.title: About this demo
paragraphs: Tandem demonstrates public pages and a project workspace using fictional records. It is a place to explore interface patterns, not a live project-management service or a support channel.
These sample terms describe that example. They do not identify a commercial operator or establish a production service agreement.

sections.title: Using the workspace
paragraphs: You can create projects, edit sample records and explore team and account settings. Changes remain in the current session and reset when you reload. The demo is not intended to store work you need to keep.
Reset demo data restores the sample records. Appearance settings are saved separately on this device and can be restored through Appearance.

sections.title: Accounts, plans and messages
paragraphs: Sign-up and recovery flows are local demonstrations. They do not create an authenticated account with a service provider. Team invitations and contact forms do not deliver messages.
Prices and plan descriptions illustrate a pricing page and selection flow. Selecting a plan does not start a subscription, create a charge or restrict the features available in the demo.

sections.title: Terms for a live service
paragraphs: A real product needs terms that reflect its operator, audience and service. Before launch, decide and document the service being offered, account responsibilities, any payment and cancellation arrangements, acceptable use, support and how disputes are handled.
Do not treat this specimen as legal advice or a ready-to-use agreement. Review the final terms against the product's actual commitments and applicable law.

questions.question: Will my changes be here after I reload?
questions.answer: Projects, account settings and team changes reset on reload. Appearance preferences are saved on this device when browser storage is available.

questions.question: What happens to an unfinished project form?
questions.answer: Navigation keeps the draft in the current session. Saving or choosing Cancel clears that form's draft. Reload and Reset demo data clear all drafts.

questions.question: Why does an open project show 100% progress?
questions.answer: Reopening a completed project changes its status but keeps its completed tasks. Status describes where the project is in the workflow; progress counts completed tasks.
